subject.title: fix(discord): default account env fallback when accounts.default.token is blank

question: Should a blank `channels.discord.accounts.default.token` inherit top-level/env fallback for the default account, or remain an explicit opt-out like named accounts?
rationale: Both choices affect shipped Discord credential semantics, SecretRef fail-closed behavior, and setup/status output, so the permanent rule needs maintainer intent before a runtime-only change lands.

options.title: Align fallback everywhere
options.body: Treat blank default-account token as inheriting top-level/env fallback, but update resolver, inspection/setup/doctor, SecretRef runtime assignment, and tests together before merge.

options.title: Keep blank token as opt-out
options.body: Reject or pause this branch and fix the config path that creates blank default-account stubs, with doctor repair if shipped configs need migration.

options.title: Accept runtime-only mitigation
options.body: Merge the narrow resolver change while knowingly accepting split status/setup and SecretRef behavior until follow-up work lands.

recommendation.title: Align fallback everywhere
recommendation.body: Treat blank default-account token as inheriting top-level/env fallback, but update resolver, inspection/setup/doctor, SecretRef runtime assignment, and tests together before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision overlaps the Discord SecretRef runtime-status work this owner authored and the credential status semantics this PR changes.
